h1: IT Performance Monitoring Services
html:
Monitoring

IT Performance Monitoring Services

CasperB2B's IT performance monitoring services watch your websites, apps, servers and network, alert the right person when something breaks or slows down, and follow up to find and fix the cause. It is for businesses that lose sales or work hours when systems go down, and that want to hear about problems before customers or staff do.

What we monitor

Uptime

Websites, portals, APIs and key services checked around the clock from outside your network.

Servers

CPU, memory, disk space, services and patch status on physical, virtual and cloud servers.

Applications

Errors, slow pages, failed jobs and response times inside the apps your business depends on.

Network

Firewalls, switches, Wi-Fi, internet links and VPNs, including drops and bandwidth spikes.

Certificates and domains

SSL certificate and domain expiry dates, so nothing lapses by surprise.

Backups

Alerts when a backup job fails or has not run, tied to your data backup and recovery plan.

How it works

  1. Map what matters. We list the systems that cost you money or time when they fail, and who should be told.
  2. Set up monitoring. We install agents and checks and connect them to your servers, apps, network gear and cloud accounts.
  3. Tune alerts. We set thresholds so real problems page someone and noise does not. Alerts go by email, text or chat.
  4. Dashboards. You get a plain dashboard showing uptime, health and recent incidents.
  5. Root-cause follow-up. After an incident we find out why it happened, fix the cause, and write a short summary.
  6. Capacity planning. We review trends regularly and tell you before disks fill, servers max out or links get too slow.

How it fits with your team

Monitoring can alert your own IT staff, our team, or both. If we run your day-to-day support through managed IT services, alerts flow straight into that work. If your apps are looked after by us under application maintenance and support, app errors go to the developers who can fix them. Recurring problems often point to a design issue, which is where IT infrastructure services come in. For marketing sites that are simply slow, see website speed optimization.

What we need from you

  • A list of systems, sites and apps to watch, or access so we can build it with you.
  • Admin or read access to servers, network gear and cloud accounts.

When this is the wrong fit

What is IT performance monitoring?

Who responds when an alert fires?

You decide. Alerts can go to your staff, to our team, or to both, based on the system and time of day.

Will we get flooded with alerts?

No. We tune thresholds during setup and after incidents so alerts point to real problems.

Can you monitor cloud services and on-site equipment together?

Yes. One dashboard can cover cloud servers, office network gear, websites and apps.

What is capacity planning?

It means reviewing usage trends so you can upgrade storage, servers or bandwidth before they become a bottleneck.

h1: Business Data Backup and Recovery Services
html:
Backup & Recovery

Business Data Backup and Recovery Services

CasperB2B's business data backup and recovery services keep copies of your files, email, servers and apps where an outage, a mistake or ransomware cannot reach them, and prove those copies restore. It is for small and mid-sized businesses that could not keep working if their data disappeared tomorrow.

The 3-2-1 approach, in plain terms

We build backups on the 3-2-1 rule: three copies of your data, on two different types of storage, with one copy kept off-site. We also keep at least one copy offline or locked so it cannot be changed or deleted, even by an attacker who gets into your network.

What we back up and set up

Servers and computers

Full and file-level backups of servers and key workstations, scheduled and checked.

Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace

Separate backups of email, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, Gmail and Drive. Built-in retention is not the same as a backup.

Cloud and offline copies

An off-site cloud copy plus an offline or immutable copy that ransomware cannot encrypt.

Apps and databases

Backups of the databases and files behind your business apps and website.

Restore testing

Scheduled test restores of files, mailboxes and whole systems, with a written result each time.

Ransomware recovery plan

A step-by-step plan for what to shut off, who to call and what to restore first.

How it works

  1. Inventory. We list where your data lives: servers, laptops, cloud apps, email and databases.
  2. Set recovery goals. For each system we agree how much data you can afford to lose and how long you can be without it.
  3. Build the backups. We set up 3-2-1 copies, encryption, retention and failure alerts.
  4. Test restores. We restore real data on a schedule and fix anything that does not come back cleanly.
  5. Write the recovery plan. You get a plain runbook for common failures, from a deleted folder to a full ransomware event.
  6. Review. We check backup reports regularly and update the plan when your systems change.

How it fits with security and IT

Backups are the last line of defense, not the only one. Pair them with small business cybersecurity services to make an attack less likely, and use our free incident response plan template so your team knows its first moves. To see what a real incident looks like, read what happens if my small business gets hacked. Backup alerts can feed into IT performance monitoring, and day-to-day care fits under managed IT services.

What we need from you

  • Admin access to your servers, Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, and key apps.
  • A short list of the data you could not work without.
  • A contact who approves the recovery plan and joins a test restore.

When this is the wrong fit

If you only need to sync a few files to the cloud, a built-in sync tool may be enough, though sync is not a backup. And if you want backups set up once and never tested, we are not the right partner: an untested backup is a guess.

FAQ

Isn't Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace already backed up?

Not fully. They keep your service running, but deleted or encrypted data may only be kept for a limited time. A separate backup gives you your own copy.

What is the 3-2-1 backup rule?

Keep three copies of your data on two types of storage, with one copy off-site. We add an offline or locked copy for ransomware protection.

Can backups stop ransomware?

No, but an offline or locked copy lets you restore without paying. Prevention comes from your cybersecurity controls.

How do we know the backups work?

We run scheduled test restores and give you a written result each time.

What happens first if we get hit?

Follow your recovery plan: isolate affected systems, call us, then restore in the priority order we agreed.

Not sure your backups would actually restore? Book a 15-minute fit call and we will check.

Staffing is broader. It covers contract work, project teams, and permanent hires who join your payroll. Many clients use both: a Casper VA for steady daily work, and a staffing engagement for a project or a permanent seat.

ModelBest whenWho employs the personHow it ends

html:
Contingent staffing

Contingent Staffing Services for Peaks, Projects and Gaps

Contingent staffing services from CasperB2B give you contract workers for a set period instead of permanent hires. It is for businesses with busy seasons, short projects, backlogs, or leave coverage that need skilled people now without adding long-term headcount.

When contingent staffing makes sense

Seasonal peaks

Extra hands for a rollout, a migration weekend, an audit, or a busy quarter.

Backlogs

A ticket queue, data cleanup, or testing backlog that your team cannot clear alongside daily work.

Coverage

Parental leave, a resignation, or a long vacancy while you search for a permanent hire.

Specialist skills

A skill you need for weeks, not years, such as a security review or a cloud cutover.

Who handles what

Contract workers are engaged through CasperB2B. In general, we handle the worker's pay and the employment paperwork tied to it. You direct the day-to-day work, approve hours, and provide access and equipment. The exact split of responsibilities, including any compliance items specific to your industry, is written into the signed scope before anyone starts.

How it works

  1. Define the need. On the fit call we cover the work, the skills, the start date, and how long you expect to need help.
  2. Scope. We put roles, schedule, approval of hours, and notice terms in a signed scope.
  3. Match. We source and screen contract workers for the skills in the scope, with a skills check for technical roles.
  4. Start. You approve the people, we coordinate start dates, and you give them access.
  5. Scale. When volume changes, tell us. We add people, extend contracts, or wind roles down under the notice terms you agreed to.

Scaling up and down

The point of a contingent workforce is flexibility. Adding a worker follows the same screening steps as the first one. Reducing headcount is a conversation with us, not a layoff on your side. If a contract worker becomes essential, you can talk to us about converting them to a direct hire.

If you need one person full time on ongoing work, a dedicated Casper VA is often a better match. See all remote roles and the ROI math.

When it is the wrong fit

Contingent staffing is not the right tool for roles at the center of your business that need long-term ownership. It also struggles when the work changes every day with no clear direction. In those cases, hire permanently or define the work first. For a defined deliverable with an end date, project staffing may be the better structure.

Frequently asked questions

What is contingent staffing?

It is the use of contract workers engaged for a set period or a specific need, instead of permanent employees.

Who pays the contract worker?

In general, CasperB2B handles the worker's pay and related paperwork, and you approve hours. The details are written into your signed scope.

How quickly can I scale down?

Under the notice terms in your scope. We agree on those terms before work starts so there are no surprises.

Can a contract worker become permanent?

Yes. Conversion terms can be included in the scope so you know the path from the start.

Describe your peak or gap on a 15-minute fit call.

  3. Signed scope. The scope names the roles, the timeline, who directs the work, and what the handoff includes.

  6. Handoff. Before roll-off, the team documents what they built and walks your people through it.

How it fits with your team

Your project owner sets priorities and approves the work. The project team works inside your tools and process. If you would rather hand off the whole deliverable to us, see our delivered services, such as custom app development, cloud migration, or software testing.

When it is the wrong fit

If the project has no defined goal or end date yet, project staffing will drift. Define the outcome first. If the work never really ends, a contingent or dedicated remote model is the better choice.

Frequently asked questions

What is project staffing?

It is staffing a defined project with the roles it needs, for the length of that project, with a planned handoff at the end.

Who manages the project team?

Your project owner directs the work. We handle staffing, check-ins, and replacing a role if the fit is wrong.

The team documents its work, transfers knowledge to your staff, and rolls off on the date in the scope.

Can the timeline change?

Yes. If a phase moves, we adjust start and roll-off dates with you under the scope terms.

Hire Train Deploy Staffing: Talent Trained on Your Stack

Cloud staffing

Cloud Engineer Staffing for AWS, Azure and GCP

CasperB2B cloud engineer staffing places AWS, Azure, and GCP engineers, DevOps engineers, cloud security engineers, and cloud architects in your business. It is for companies migrating to the cloud, running production workloads, or cleaning up cloud accounts that grew without a plan.

Roles we staff

Cloud engineers

Build and run infrastructure on AWS, Azure, or GCP: networking, compute, storage, identity, and cost controls.

DevOps engineers

CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, containers, and the release process your developers rely on.

Cloud security engineers

Access policies, logging, configuration reviews, and hardening across your cloud accounts.

Cloud architects

Design the target environment, plan migrations, and set standards your team can follow.

How it works

  1. Environment intake. We learn your cloud provider, current setup, tools, and the first problems the engineer will own.
  2. Sourcing. We search for engineers with hands-on experience on your provider and tools.
  3. Technical assessment. A provider-specific exercise or design discussion: troubleshooting a broken deployment, reviewing an access policy, or sketching a migration plan.
  4. Shortlist and interviews. You meet a short list with our notes. We schedule interviews and collect feedback.
  5. Start. We coordinate access, start dates, and check in after the first weeks.

Choose the right engagement

  • A migration with an end date: project staffing.
  • Extra hands during a busy period: contingent staffing.
  • A permanent cloud owner: direct hire.
  • A full-time remote engineer that CasperB2B employs and manages: dedicated cloud network engineer.

If you want the migration done for you rather than staffed, see cloud migration services and IT infrastructure.

What we need from you

Tell us which provider you use, what is already built, and who the engineer will report to. Have accounts and access ready for day one. For security roles, tell us which policies or frameworks you work under so we screen for them.

When it is the wrong fit

If you run a small office with a few cloud apps and no custom infrastructure, you likely do not need a cloud engineer. Managed IT will cover it.

Frequently asked questions

What does cloud engineer staffing include?

Sourcing, screening, a provider-specific technical assessment, shortlist, interviews, and start coordination for cloud, DevOps, cloud security, and architect roles.

Do you staff all three major clouds?

Yes. We screen for AWS, Azure, or GCP based on what you run.

Can I hire a cloud engineer just for a migration?

Yes. Project staffing covers a migration with a defined end date and handoff.

Do you staff cloud security roles?

Yes. Tell us which policies or frameworks apply and we screen for them.

Describe your cloud setup on a 15-minute fit call.

h1: IT Staffing and Services for Telecom Companies
html:
Telecom

IT Staffing and Services for Telecom Companies

CasperB2B provides IT staffing and services for telecom companies: dedicated network, NOC, field support and software people, plus infrastructure and monitoring work, for carriers, ISPs, fiber builders and telecom service providers that need skilled hands without a long hiring cycle.

We are founder-led and work remotely with telecom teams across the U.S. and worldwide. You get a personal reply within 1 business day, and every engagement starts from a signed scope.

Who this is for

Regional ISPs, wireless and fiber operators, VoIP and unified communications providers, tower and field service firms, and telecom software vendors. Most come to us for one of three reasons: a backlog of network or support tickets, a build-out or migration that needs extra people for a set period, or monitoring that only works when someone remembers to look.

What telecom work is really like

Telecom teams run networks that customers expect to be up all the time. Outages are public, maintenance windows fall at night, and one bad change can affect thousands of subscribers. Work is spread across the NOC, the field, the core network and the billing and provisioning systems. Skills are specific: routing and switching, fiber and wireless, SIP and voice, OSS/BSS software. Hiring for those skills is slow, and project peaks rarely line up with headcount plans.

What we provide

Network and NOC staffing

Dedicated network engineers and NOC technicians who watch alarms, work tickets, run escalations and document changes. See IT staffing and our network engineer role.

Field and support roles

Tier 1 and tier 2 support, dispatch coordination, and remote help for field crews. Our remote IT support engineers handle tickets in your system, under your process.

Infrastructure work

Planning, standing up and documenting servers, cloud resources, firewalls and internal systems that keep operations running. See IT infrastructure services.

Monitoring and alerting

Uptime, latency and capacity checks with alert rules your team agrees on, so problems reach the right person. See performance monitoring.

Software and QA people

Developers and QA engineers for provisioning tools, customer portals, billing integrations and internal apps.

Project teams

A defined group for a migration, a system cutover or a backlog cleanup, sized for the project and released when it ends. See project staffing.

How engagement works

  1. Fit call. A 15-minute call to learn the role or project, your tools, and your hours of coverage.
  2. Signed scope. We write down the roles, skills, schedule, access needs and how success is measured.
  3. Candidates or plan. For staffing, you interview candidates before anyone starts. For infrastructure or monitoring work, you approve a written plan first.
  4. Onboarding. Your team grants access through your own accounts and change process. We follow your runbooks and escalation paths.
  5. Regular review. We check in on ticket quality, coverage gaps and open issues, and adjust the scope when your needs change.

When we are the wrong fit

We are not a tower crew or a cable installation contractor, and we do not supply licensed on-site technicians for physical work. If you need people to climb, splice or pull cable in person, hire a local field contractor. We are also a poor fit if you want staff with no onboarding from your side. Every person we place needs access, a point of contact and your procedures.

Telecom IT staffing FAQ

Can your people cover nights and weekends?

Yes, coverage hours are part of the scope. We agree on shifts and escalation rules before anyone starts.

Do your engineers work in our ticketing and monitoring tools?

Yes. They work in your systems with accounts you control, so you keep the history and can remove access at any time.

Can we start with one role and add more later?

Yes. Many teams start with one network or support role, then add people for a project through project staffing.

Do you handle telecom software development too?

Yes. We build and maintain internal tools and portals through our custom app development work, scoped like any other project.

How fast can someone start?

It depends on the role and how quickly you can interview and grant access. We give you a realistic timeline on the fit call.

If you have a network backlog or a project that needs people, book a 15-minute fit call and we will tell you plainly whether we can help.

title: Healthcare IT Services for Practices | CasperB2B

h1: Healthcare IT Services for Practices and Clinics
html:
Healthcare

Healthcare IT Services for Practices and Clinics

CasperB2B provides healthcare IT services for medical practices, clinics, dental offices and other care providers: managed IT, security practices built with HIPAA in mind, backup and recovery, staffing for healthcare IT roles, and patient-facing websites.

We are founder-led and work remotely with providers in the U.S., with a local focus in Massachusetts and New Hampshire. You get a personal reply within 1 business day, and work starts from a signed scope.

Who this is for

Independent practices, multi-location clinics, dental groups, behavioral health offices, physical therapy and specialty practices, and med spas. It also fits healthcare software and service companies that need IT or development people. Most have no full-time IT staff, or one person who is stretched too thin.

What healthcare IT is really like

A clinic cannot stop seeing patients because a computer is down. Front desk systems, the EHR, phones, scanners and payment devices all have to work at once. Patient data is sensitive and regulated, staff turn over, and many offices still share passwords or run old machines. Ransomware and phishing target healthcare because downtime is so costly. Good IT here is mostly steady habits: access control, patching, backups that are tested, and clear records of who can see what.

What we provide

Managed IT for the office

Help desk, device setup, patching, and vendor coordination for your EHR, phones and printers. See managed IT services.

Security practices

Multi-factor sign-in, user access reviews, email filtering, device encryption and staff phishing training. See cybersecurity services.

Backup and recovery

Backups of servers, cloud files and key systems, with restore tests on a schedule and a written recovery plan. See backup and recovery.

Healthcare IT staffing

Dedicated IT support, security and development people who work inside your tools. See IT staffing.

Patient-facing websites

Fast, mobile-friendly sites with clear service pages and booking paths, built without putting patient data in web forms that should not hold it. See website development and dental practice marketing.

Incident planning

A simple plan for what staff do if an account is taken over or files are locked. Start with our incident response plan template.

How HIPAA fits in

We set up IT and security practices with HIPAA requirements in mind, and we work with your compliance lead or privacy officer on the technical safeguards. We do not certify practices, and we do not guarantee compliance. Your organization remains responsible for its own compliance program, including risk assessments, policies, training records and business associate agreements. Where our work involves access to patient data, we discuss the right agreement before work begins.

How engagement works

  1. Fit call. Fifteen minutes on your systems, your biggest risks and who owns compliance.
  2. Review. We look at accounts, devices, backups and network setup and write down what we find.
  3. Signed scope. You approve a prioritized list of fixes and ongoing services.
  4. Fixes first. We close the highest-risk gaps, such as missing sign-in protection or untested backups.
  5. Ongoing care. Support, monitoring and regular reviews with your compliance lead.

When we are the wrong fit

We are not a compliance auditor or law firm, and we do not replace legal advice. Large hospital systems with in-house IT departments and dedicated compliance teams usually need a different kind of partner. We are also not the right choice if you want a vendor to take over all compliance responsibility.

Healthcare IT services FAQ

Are you HIPAA certified?

There is no official government HIPAA certification for IT providers. We follow HIPAA-aware practices and work with your compliance lead, and your practice remains responsible for its compliance program.

Will you sign a business associate agreement?

When our work involves access to patient data, we discuss a business associate agreement during scoping, before work begins.

Do you support our EHR?

We support the devices, accounts and network around your EHR and coordinate with the EHR vendor, who supports the software itself.

Can you test our backups?

Yes. Restore tests are part of our backup and recovery work, so you know files and systems can actually come back.

Do you build patient websites too?

Yes. We build fast, mobile-friendly sites and keep forms limited to what is safe to collect online.

If your practice needs steadier IT or a security check, book a 15-minute fit call and we will tell you where to start.

h1: IT Staffing for Government Contractors
html:
Government contractors

IT Staffing for Government Contractors

CasperB2B provides IT staffing for government contractors: dedicated developers, QA engineers, IT support, network and security engineers, and project teams for companies that deliver work to federal, state and local agencies.

We are founder-led and work remotely with contractors in the U.S. You get a personal reply within 1 business day, and every engagement starts from a signed scope.

Who this is for

Prime contractors and subcontractors that deliver software, IT support, help desk, cloud or security work to public agencies. It also fits contractors that need internal IT support for their own offices and staff while their billable team stays focused on the contract.

What government contracting is really like

Contract work runs on defined scopes, deliverables and reporting. Awards can come with tight start dates, and option years or new task orders can change staffing needs fast. Many roles carry requirements set by the agency: citizenship, background checks, security clearances, on-site work, or specific training. Security expectations are high, and documentation matters as much as the work itself. Contractors need people who follow process and keep good records.

What we provide

Contract IT staffing

Dedicated technical people placed on your team for a role or a period of performance. See IT staffing and contingent staffing.

Developers and QA

Developers and QA engineers for application builds, maintenance and test work. See software testing and application maintenance.

Security and network engineers

People who harden systems, review access, watch alerts and document controls. See our security engineer and network engineer roles.

Help desk and IT support

Remote support for end users, device setup and ticket handling. See remote IT support.

Project teams

A defined group for a migration, a deliverable or a surge in work, sized to the task. See project staffing.

Your own company IT

Managed IT and security for your internal systems, so your offices run well. See managed IT and cybersecurity services.

Clearances and contract vehicles

Whether a role needs a security clearance, U.S. citizenship, on-site presence or other screening depends on the agency, the contract and the role. CasperB2B does not hold a facility clearance, security certifications or any contract vehicle, and we do not claim to. We work as a staffing and IT partner to the contractor that holds the contract. On the fit call we go through each role's requirements, and we only take on roles we can fill as written.

How engagement works

  1. Fit call. Fifteen minutes on the roles, start dates and requirements your contract sets.
  2. Signed scope. We write down each role, the skills, the screening needs and the schedule.
  3. Candidates. You review and interview candidates before anyone starts.
  4. Onboarding. You grant access through your process and train on your procedures and reporting.
  5. Check-ins. We review performance and staffing needs as the contract changes.

When we are the wrong fit

If a role needs an active security clearance, on-site work at an agency facility, or a sponsor relationship we cannot provide, we will say so and you should use a cleared staffing firm. We are also not a proposal writer or a contracts advisor, and we cannot help you win an award or get on a contract vehicle.

Government contractor IT staffing FAQ

Do you provide cleared staff?

Not by default. Clearance needs depend on the role and contract, and we only take on cleared roles if we can meet the requirement as written.

Does CasperB2B hold a GSA schedule or other contract vehicle?

No. We work as a staffing and IT partner to the contractor that holds the contract.

Can your people work remotely on our contract?

It depends on the contract terms. Many support, development and testing roles allow remote work, but some require on-site or U.S.-based staff.

Can we add people when a new task order starts?

Yes. Staffing levels are part of the scope and can change as your contract does.

Do you also support our company's own IT?

Yes. We offer managed IT and security for your internal systems, separate from contract staffing.

If you have roles to fill on a contract, book a 15-minute fit call and we will tell you honestly which ones we can cover.
